AT HOME

Can I open the windows?

When haze gets worse

Keep windows and outside doors closed to reduce the particles coming in. A suitable air purifier can help with indoor particles; a fan or air-conditioning helps with comfort.

When the outside air improves

Air the room periodically. Check conditions near your home as well as the regional reading. A “Normal” band does not mean the air is pollution-free.

If the room gets hot or stuffy

Do not leave the room sealed indefinitely. Closed rooms can build up heat, carbon dioxide and other pollutants. Use a cooler indoor space if needed, and ventilate when outdoor conditions improve.

The window card is our cautious interpretation: at 56 µg/m³ and above, it suggests keeping windows closed for now; at 0–55, it asks you to check local conditions before airing the room. NEA does not set an official one-hour window-opening cutoff. Regional readings cannot tell us whether the air inside your home is cleaner. A clear sky or lack of smoke smell is not proof that the air is clean.

03 / THE SHORT GUIDE

What the numbers mean

How to use PM2.5 and PSI when planning your day.

01

PM2.5 for the next hour

These tiny particles can get deep into your lungs. The 1-hour reading tells you how much was in the air over the past hour. It can change quickly, so check again before heading out.

02

PSI for the longer view

Singapore’s 24-hour PSI is an air-quality index based on several pollutants. The reading shown here describes recent conditions. For tomorrow’s outing, check NEA’s forecast and advisory.

03

Why other apps differ

Countries calculate “AQI” differently. This site uses NEA’s original Singapore readings and bands. Compare the pollutant, averaging period and source before comparing two numbers.

N95 · KN95 · KF94 · FFP2

04 / A PRACTICAL MASK GUIDE

Choose a mask that fits

MOH includes N95, KN95, KF94 and FFP2 as options for haze particles. A genuine, well-fitting model from these groups is a practical starting point when a respirator is needed.

  • ✓A short commute? MOH says a respirator is generally unnecessary for routine commuting or indoors. Follow the current band and your health needs.
  • ✓Check the seal every time. Cover your nose and mouth fully, mould the nosepiece, and follow the maker’s seal-check instructions. Gaps and facial hair at the seal reduce protection.
  • ✓Buy a small pack first. Compare the delivered price per mask after finding a certified model that seals comfortably. Surgical fluid resistance adds no particle-filtration benefit for haze.
Read MOH’s mask guidance ↗

What the filtration labels actually mean

Compare masks: ratings, fit and cost

These are minimum filter efficiencies under each standard’s laboratory tests, not the percentage of protection you will get on your face. Standards use different test conditions; fit and authenticity matter. A “95% BFE” surgical mask is not the same as an N95.

NOT A HAZE RESPIRATOR

Cloth / fashion / paper

No fixed rating

Material and leakage vary. Uncertified “PM2.5” inserts do not establish protection for the whole mask.

Value for haze: avoid spending on these as your particle protection.

LOOSE FIT

Surgical / 3-ply / KF-AD

BFE ≠ respirator rating

Designed mainly for droplets and splashes. A bacterial filtration claim does not tell you how much haze leaks around the edges.

Value for haze: low purchase price does not make it a substitute for a respirator.

PRACTICAL HAZE OPTION

N95

≥95% NIOSH · US

Often uses two headbands. Check the NIOSH name, model and TC approval number. A standard N95 and surgical N95 have the same minimum particle rating.

Value for haze: a useful choice if it seals well; no need to pay for a surgical version solely for haze.

PRACTICAL HAZE OPTION

KN95

≥95% GB 2626 · China

Commonly sold in folding designs. Ear loops or headbands vary by model; verify the stated standard and check for gaps.

Value for haze: compare it with N95 on genuine certification, your fit and price per mask.

PRACTICAL HAZE OPTION

KF94

≥94% MFDS · Korea

Commonly sold in boat shapes. Look for a genuine KF94 product and the correct size. The standard differs from N95, though MOH accepts it for haze.

Value for haze: a practical option if it fits; the one-point rating difference alone should not decide your purchase.

PRACTICAL HAZE OPTION

FFP2

≥94% EN 149 · Europe

A tight-fitting particulate respirator. Check the EN 149 classification and manufacturer’s markings; shape and straps vary.

Value for haze: another suitable category; choose a certified fit rather than paying for an imported label.

Other ratings, reusable respirators and valves
KF80: ≥80%

A lower filtration class. It is not one of MOH’s listed N95-equivalent haze options; select N95, KN95, KF94 or FFP2 when that level of protection is called for.

N99 / FFP3 / KF99: ≥99%

Higher filter ratings with different certification tests. Buying one is optional, not an official requirement triggered by a particular PM2.5 band. A poor seal still lets particles in.

N100 / P100: ≥99.97%

P-series filters also resist oil aerosols. These higher filter classes are not required by MOH’s general haze guide. Balance cost, fit and comfort before upgrading.

Reusable half-face respirators

The fitted filter determines the particle rating. Include replacement filters, cleaning and storage in the cost; follow the manufacturer’s service-life instructions. A gas cartridge alone is not a particulate filter.

Valved vs unvalved

A valve can ease exhalation; it does not increase the stated filter rating. Outward air may bypass filtration, so an unvalved model is the simpler choice when protecting others from respiratory infections also matters.

“Carbon” and “anti-odour” masks

Carbon is not a particle certification. Check for a recognised respirator rating. Particle respirators do not protect against all haze gases or vapours.

Rating sources: HSA mask comparison, NIOSH filter classes, 3M standards comparison, MFDS KF ratings, HSE FFP3 comparison.

Which mask, at which haze level?

Use the 1-hour PM2.5 reading for immediate plans. These practical choices follow MOH’s activity guidance; the value notes are our editorial suggestions, not product endorsements.

Mask choices for all four haze levels
Normal · 0–55 µg/m³

Keep your normal plans

Ordinary activities can continue. A respirator is generally unnecessary for a short commute or indoors.

Value move: keep a small supply ready rather than wearing a new mask routinely for normal air.

Elevated · 56–150 µg/m³

Ease off strenuous exercise

Healthy adults should reduce strenuous outdoor activity; higher-risk people should avoid it.

Value move: shorten or move the workout indoors. A higher-rated mask is not a reason to push through.

High · 151–250 µg/m³

Skip strenuous outdoor activity

Higher-risk people should avoid all outdoor activity. If exposure is unavoidable, a well-fitting N95 or equivalent can reduce particles inhaled; this is also relevant for prolonged exposure.

Value move: use a genuine, well-fitting N95 / KN95 / KF94 / FFP2 you can afford.

Very high · ≥251 µg/m³

Minimise time outdoors

Higher-risk people should avoid outdoor activity. For unavoidable time outside, consider a well-fitting N95 or equivalent.

Value move: prioritise less exposure and a reliable seal. MOH does not require an N99 or P100 upgrade.

Make the protection count

Follow the maker’s use and replacement instructions. Replace a mask when damaged, dirty, damp or difficult to breathe through; do not wash disposable respirators. Do not share them. For children, adult masks may not seal: prioritise staying indoors and ask a healthcare professional about suitable protection. Older adults, pregnant people and people with severe heart or lung problems who have difficulty breathing should consult a doctor about respirator use. If you feel unwell, seek medical advice.

Guidance checked 17 October 2026. Check MOH for updates.

05 / SMALL, USEFUL MOVES

A little less exposure.

Move the workout in

Swap the run for an indoor session when the air is elevated or high.

Make indoors more comfortable

During sustained haze, close windows and use air filtration if available.

Check again before leaving

Haze can shift within hours. A fresh reading is more useful than a screenshot from earlier.
